A.explanation: About $49 \text{ Hz}$ is only the increase on approach, $649 - 600$, not the full change from approaching to receding.

B.explanation: About $84 \text{ Hz}$ is too small and does not match $f_0v/(v-v_s) - f_0v/(v+v_s)$ with $f_0 = 600 \text{ Hz}$, $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: The difference between $600 \times 330/305 \approx 649 \text{ Hz}$ on approach and $600 \times 330/355 \approx 558 \text{ Hz}$ on recession is about $91 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: About $98 \text{ Hz}$ is twice the approaching increase, which wrongly assumes the decrease on recession equals the increase on approach.

hints: Notice the two limiting cases: a long way behind means the $25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ ambulance is approaching the observer, and a long way in front means it is receding at the same speed.

Recall the Doppler observed wavelength is shortened on approach and lengthened on recession, so use $f' = fv/(v-v_s)$ for approaching and $f' = fv/(v+v_s)$ for receding with $f = 600 \text{ Hz}$ and $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate both observed frequencies separately and then subtract the lower receding frequency from the higher approaching frequency to get the overall drop.
walkthrough: Identify the two states: far to the left the ambulance moves towards the stationary observer, far to the right it moves away from the observer, both with source speed $v_s = 25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the Doppler rule for a moving source: $f' = f v/(v - v_s)$ on approach because wavefronts are crowded together, and $f' = f v/(v + v_s)$ on recession because wavefronts are spread out.
Substitute $f = 600 \text{ Hz}$ and $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for approach: $f_{approach} = 600 \times 330/(330-25) = 600 \times 330/305 \approx 649.2 \text{ Hz}$.
Find the overall change as the drop from the high approaching pitch to the low receding pitch: $\Delta f \approx 649.2 - 557.7 \approx 91.5 \text{ Hz}$, about $91 \text{ Hz}$. This is option C.
